_what: Laughingstock, a comedy club on the street. The stage is our own Disabled Comedy playlist, put on whole; the bill under it is every set on that playlist, each of which plays where it hangs or goes up on the stage in place of the whole night (rack.js's pattern, Ryan's ask, 2026-10-03); the acts are the two comics our Campfire Learn Together watched, with their own lines standing in the spotlight. tools/make-laughingstock.py builds all of it and the credits in liner-notes.html from this file. Do not hand-edit between the markers.
_source: The bill was first read off the playlist page's own data (ytInitialData) on 2026-09-23, and read again on 2026-10-03 with yt-dlp --flat-playlist, when the header and the list agreed and nothing was hidden. That second reading found four AJ Wilkerson specials Ryan had added since, which are on the bill now, and the sets in Ryan's brief of 2026-10-03. Titles, channels and runtimes are YouTube's and not typed from memory. Every runtime is the playlist's own figure for that set, which is what the player reports; the watch page's lengthSeconds can read a second shorter, because it is rounded down. A set not yet on the playlist takes its runtime off its watch page until it is. Every id was checked on that page the day it went on -- playabilityStatus OK, playableInEmbed true, and none of them LOGIN_REQUIRED, which is the age gate that caught one of Black Leather Lagoon's songs. The playlist's first entry is Yoa7MUa-AL0, which plays: the Queercore deck on the dancefloor failed to embed because of what sat at the top of its list, and this is the check that would have caught it. INBRED MAGIC's description tells a story about a friend, Jake, doing an improvised set, so who performs it was read off the auto-captions on 2026-10-03 rather than assumed: Jake introduces the set and AJ Wilkerson performs it and signs off by name.
_titles: The title on each set is the set's own name, trimmed of the comic's name and of words like FULL SPECIAL, because the comic is credited separately on every row and the channel's packaging is not the set. title_verbatim is exactly what YouTube shows, kept so nobody has to go and look. Where a title carries a word this room would never use in its own voice, it is still the title: it is the comic's or the channel's, and make-laughingstock.py does not sweep titles for that reason.
_order: The playlist's own order, which is Stimpunks' and is not re-sorted here. There is no headliner: a comedy bill runs opener to closer as a matter of trade, and a room whose whole argument is that disabled comics should be judged on their work has no business ranking any of them by where they stand in the running order.
_drift: The bill is a MIRROR of the playlist and it drifts by design. A set added to the playlist is on the stage the next time somebody puts the whole night on, and is not on the bill until somebody reads the playlist again and adds a row here. The room says so under the bill, with the date this file was read, rather than implying the two are the same list. It can drift the other way too: a set marked "playlist": false is on the bill and not yet on the playlist, and the room names it under the bill, because putting the whole night on will not reach it. Stuart Laws' two sets came in Ryan's brief of 2026-10-03 and were not on the playlist when it was read that day; they sit where the brief put them, and the flag comes off when the playlist has them. If a row goes dead, check-jukebox.py is what notices.
_who: Where a note says how a comic is Disabled, that is Ryan's brief of 2026-10-03 for Joe Wells, Fern Brady, Tim Renkow, Stuart Laws, Pierre Novellie, Hannah Gadsby, Lara Ricote and Rosie Jones, and AJ Wilkerson's own descriptions (Captain Autism) for AJ Wilkerson. Tim Renkow's very dark humour and Hannah Gadsby's material on gender are Ryan's notes, put where somebody reads them before the press. The notes write round pronouns rather than guess at any.
_left_off: Fern Brady on referring to autism as a 'superpower' (a Last Leg short, 4I4TYOvYyYs, on Channel 4 Entertainment) was in Ryan's brief of 2026-10-03 and is not on the bill: its watch page answered UNPLAYABLE, and yt-dlp said the uploader has not made it available in this country. A Channel 4 clip blocked outside the UK would be a button that plays for some visitors and shows a refusal to the rest, and it is not on the playlist either. Fern Brady's full special is on the bill.
_lines: Every line under an act is quoted from our own Campfire Learn Together write-up, https://stimpunks.org/2026/05/02/campfire-learn-together-being-disabled-can-be-pretty-funny/, checked word for word against the Knowledge System mirror's copy of that post on 2026-09-23, and credited to the comic whose line it is. THE WRITE-UP DOES NOT SAY WHICH SET EACH LINE COMES FROM AND THIS FILE DOES NOT GUESS. A line credited to the wrong special would be the jukebox's guessed mapping arriving at a comedy club. Where a line is somebody else speaking inside the comic's bit -- the friend at the restaurant -- the context says so.

lines.text: I’m guessing: talk with your manager.
lines.context: His friend’s answer, in his bit, when a server asked the friend what he would have.

lines.text: well, fuck cerebral palsy, we could really be helping people.
lines.context: On Botox, and on who medical research turns out to be for.

lines.text: I don’t suffer from cerebral palsy, I suffer from people
lines.context: The social model of disability, compressed into a punchline.
One of the three perks of being a disabled comic: she can never be a hack.
Not fully committed to either side, which is where a great many of us live.
